is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on the major malaria vector Anopheles funestus sampled in Cameroon, Malawi, and Uganda (p. 2-3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports the target marker Cyp9k1 G454A (page 9: 'Analysis of the coding region detected a non-synonymous polymorphism, substituting glycine for alanine at position 454...').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Allele/genotype counts for Cyp9k1 G454A are reported on page 9: 'a mutation which is present in all individuals from Uganda. This G454A change was detected at lower frequencies in Malawi (14/40) and in Cameroon (9/40)' with 20 mosquitoes (40 alleles) genotyped per country.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Mibellon, Cameroon (Feb 2015), Tororo, Uganda (March 2014), and Chikwawa, Malawi (Jan 2014), and tested as F1 adults (p. 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study combining multi-omics genomic analysis and functional validation in Anopheles funestus (p. 1-3).

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific collection sites with geographical coordinates are given: Mibellon (6°46′N, 11°70′E), Cameroon; Tororo (0°45′N, 34°5′E), Uganda; Chikwawa (16°1′S, 34°47′E), Malawi (p. 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in February 2015 (Cameroon), March 2014 (Uganda), and January 2014 (Malawi) (p. 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Page 3 notes: 'Insecticide resistance bioassays on these samples have been previously described (Mulamba, Riveron, et al., 2014; Riveron et al., 2015, 2016).' The mosquito samples originate from these previously published field collections.

supplement.evidence: Allele counts and frequencies for the target marker Cyp9k1 G454A across Uganda, Malawi, and Cameroon are explicitly provided in the main text (p. 9).

assessment.summary: This study uses multi-omics and functional validation to investigate pyrethroid resistance in Anopheles funestus from Cameroon, Malawi, and Uganda. Target-enrichment sequencing identified the CYP9K1 G454A mutation, which was fixed in Ugandan mosquitoes (40/40 alleles) and present at lower frequencies in Malawi (14/40) and Cameroon (9/40). Recombinant CYP9K1 heterologously expressed in E. coli metabolised deltamethrin (64% depletion).
